'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Southern Ukraine offensive]]
****[[Bombing of Odesa (2022–present)|Battle of Odesa]]
*****Large explosions are reported in the port city of [[Odesa]] as residents are urged to seek shelter. Ukrainian officials say the [[Russian Air Force]] has fired missiles at the city, and that some [[missile]]s have been intercepted. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-europe-60949706 (BBC News)] [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/ukraine-russia-crisis-air-strikes-hit-ukraines-strategic-black-sea-port-odessa-2859688 (NDTV)]
***[[Bucha massacre]], [[War crimes in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
****[[Human Rights Watch]], an independent [[human rights]] group, says that it has documented allegations of [[war crime]]s perpetrated by [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] in [[Ukraine]] against civilians, including [[rape]], [[summary execution]], and [[looting]] of civilian properties. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-04-3-22/h_d8455329a6510ce26701a51d2b0d6eef (CNN)]
****The [[United States]], the [[European Union]], and [[NATO]] leaders react to emerging reports of the massacre in Bucha, accusing the Russian Armed Forces of war crimes and calling for more sanctions against Russia. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-europe-60949706 (BBC News)]
*[[Afghanistan conflict]]
**One person is killed and several more are injured after a militant bombs a money exchange hub in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]]. While the [[Taliban]] says that ten people were injured, the city's emergency hospital counts an injury toll of 59. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/blast-afghan-capital-kills-one-wounds-dozens-health-workers-2022-04-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Twenty-one people are killed during an [[Allied Democratic Forces|ADF]] attack at the village of Masambo, in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/suspected-islamists-kill-21-civilians-eastern-congo-2022-04-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[64th Annual Grammy Awards]]
**During the ceremony, [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] makes a video appearance and delivers a pre-taped speech urging viewers to support his country during the invasion in "any way" they can. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/volodymyr-zelensky-ukraine-video-appearance-2022-grammys-1235124372/amp/ (''The Hollywood Reporter'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/arts-entertainment/2022/04/03/zelensky-grammy-awards-appearance/ (''The Washington Post'')]
  
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Shanghai]]
****Around 25 million residents in [[Shanghai]] are ordered to undergo [[COVID-19 testing]] in an effort to contain the current [[COVID-19]] outbreak. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3172914/shanghai-orders-covid-tests-all-25-million-residents-bid (''South China Morning Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2022 Sacramento shooting]]
**Six people are killed and 12 others are injured during a [[mass shooting]] at a popular nightlife area in [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]], [[California]], [[United States]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/multiple-people-shot-downtown-sacramento-california-police/story?id=83843793 (ABC News)]
*[[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]
**Around ten people are injured in downtown [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina|Chapel Hill]], [[North Carolina]], after a series of riots broke out following [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|UNC]]'s victory against [[2021–22 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the Final Four. [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2022/04/03/us/north-carolina-chapel-hill-unc-ncaa-celebrations/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Hungarian parliamentary election]]
**Voters in [[Hungary]] head to the polls to elect a new [[National Assembly (Hungary)|National Assembly]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/03/hungary-votes-general-election-viktor-orban (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Fidesz]], the party of current [[Prime Minister of Hungary|Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]], wins most of the seats and retains its parliamentary supermajority, while opposition leader [[Péter Márki-Zay]] loses his home district of [[Hódmezővásárhely]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/04/03/europe/hungary-election-results-viktor-orban-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2022 Serbian general election]]
**Voters in [[Serbia]] head to the polls to vote in the presidential and parliamentary elections. [https://www.dw.com/en/serbian-elections-aleksandar-vucics-media-dominance-aids-bid-for-another-term/a-61322314 (DW)]
**[[President of Serbia|President]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] is re-elected with 60.0% of the vote, and his party [[Serbian Progressive Party]] wins the most votes in the [[National Assembly (Serbia)|National Assembly]] at 42.9% though fail to win an overall majority of seats. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/serbians-go-polls-pick-president-parliament-amid-ukraine-war-2022-04-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Costa Rican general election]]
**Voters in [[Costa Rica]] head to the polls to vote in the second round of the presidential election. [https://www.tse.go.cr/2022/escrutinio.html (TSE)]
**[[Rodrigo Chaves Robles]] is elected [[President of Costa Rica]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/costa-ricans-choose-between-outsider-former-leader-presidential-vote-2022-04-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Pakistani constitutional crisis]]
**[[President of Pakistan|Pakistani President]] [[Arif Alvi]] dissolves the [[National Assembly of Pakistan|National Assembly]] after [[Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan|Deputy Speaker]] [[Qasim Suri]] refused to hold a [[motion of no confidence]] against [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Prime Minister]] [[Imran Khan]], who was widely expected to lose the motion. Khan previously accused the [[United States]] of conspiring with the opposition to remove him due to his opposition towards US foreign policy, which the US denies. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-60972186 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Sri Lankan protests]]
**The [[Second Gotabaya Rajapaksa cabinet|entire cabinet]] of [[Prime Minister of Sri Lanka|Prime Minister]] [[Mahinda Rajapaksa]] resigns following days of economic protests in [[Sri Lanka]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-60975941 (BBC News)]
*Former [[Crown Prince of Jordan]] [[Hamzah bin Hussein]] announces on [[Twitter]] that he is renouncing his "Prince" title, saying that his "personal convictions" are not in line with the "modern methods of our institutions". Hamzah has been under house arrest [[2021 arrests in Jordan|since last March]] after he accused [[Jordan]]ian leaders of corruption and incompetence. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-60976314 (BBC News)]
